intro.p: Let \vec{v}= {{v}} and \mathcal B=\{\vec b_1,\vec b_2,\vec b_3\,\vec b_4\} where \vec b_1 = {{b_1}}, \vec b_2= {{b_2}}, \vec b_3 = {{b_3}}, and \vec b_4 = {{b_4}}..

content.p: Explain and demonstrate how to verify that \mathcal{B} is a basis of \mathbb R^4 and how to calculate P_\mathcal{B}, the change-of-basis matrix from the standard basis of \mathbb R^4 to \mathcal{B}.
Explain and demonstrate how to use P_\mathcal{B} to express \vec{v} in the new coordinate system \{\vec{v}\}_{\mathcal{B}}.
Explain and demonstrate how to find \vec{y} if {y}_{\mathcal{B}}={{y_b}}
